# attrakttv

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

A Shiny app for browsing TV show episode ratings, built on
[{tRakt}](https://github.com/jemus42/tRakt) and the
[trakt.tv](https://trakt.tv) API.

The app caches show / season / episode data in a local SQLite database so
repeat lookups are fast, and visualises per-episode rating trajectories
with [plotly](https://plotly.com/r/).

> attrakttv is an unofficial fan project and is **not affiliated with,
> endorsed by, or connected to trakt.tv**.

## Installation

```r
# pak (recommended) — pulls in the {tRakt} GitHub remote automatically
pak::pak("jemus42/attrakttv")

# or remotes
remotes::install_github("jemus42/attrakttv")
```

## Usage

```r
attrakttv::attrakttv_app()
```

By default the app listens on **http://127.0.0.1:7842** and opens in your
browser. Override with the `port` argument or the `attrakttv.port` option.

Cached data is stored in a SQLite database under the platform-appropriate
data directory (`rappdirs::user_data_dir("attrakttv", <version>)`):

| Platform | Default path |
|----------|--------------|
| macOS    | `~/Library/Application Support/attrakttv/<version>/tRakt.db` |
| Linux    | `~/.local/share/attrakttv/<version>/tRakt.db` |
| Windows  | `%LOCALAPPDATA%/attrakttv/attrakttv/<version>/tRakt.db` |

Set the `trakt_db_path` environment variable to override the directory.

### API credentials

- **trakt.tv:** not required for normal read-only use — `{tRakt}` ships
  with a scrambled fallback client_secret since 0.17.0, so basic data
  retrieval works out of the box. Set `trakt_client_id` /
  `trakt_client_secret` in your `~/.Renviron` if you want your own quota.
- **fanart.tv:** required to fetch poster images. Sign up at
  <https://fanart.tv/get-an-api-key/>, then set `fanarttv_api_key` in your
  `~/.Renviron`. See `attrakttv.env-sample` for the variable names.

Sourcing the included `attrakttv.env-sample` instead of `~/.Renviron` also
works — it is recognised by `Sys.getenv()` when copied to `.Renviron` in
the working directory.

## Features

- Search any TV show by title and see per-show metadata, season summary,
  and per-episode ratings.
- Caches results to SQLite so subsequent lookups are instant.
- Built with [{bslib}](https://rstudio.github.io/bslib/) on Bootstrap 5
  with light/dark mode toggle.
- Stable URL per show via query params (e.g. `?show=counterpart`).

## Development

```sh
make install      # pak::local_install
make launch       # launch the installed app on port 7842
make launch-dev   # devtools::load_all + run against /tmp/attrakttv-smoke-db
make document     # devtools::document
make check        # devtools::check
```

`make launch-dev` uses a throwaway SQLite db at `/tmp/attrakttv-smoke-db`
so it never pollutes your real cache.

## Deployment (horst)

The repo doubles as the on-host service folder under `~/docker/attrakttv/`
on [horst](https://horst.jemu.name), following the one-folder-per-service
Docker convention used for every other app on that box. State
(`./data/tRakt.db`) and secrets (`.env`) live next to `docker-compose.yml`.

### First deploy

```sh
ssh horst
git clone https://github.com/jemus42/attrakttv.git ~/docker/attrakttv
cd ~/docker/attrakttv
cp attrakttv.env-sample .env
$EDITOR .env                   # plug in fanarttv_api_key (required)
mkdir -p data
docker compose up -d --build
```

The image pins the in-container `attrakttv` user to UID/GID **1000** so the
bind-mounted `./data/` is writable when the host operator's UID is also 1000
(the Debian default and what horst uses). If your host UID differs, build
with explicit arg overrides:

```sh
docker compose build \
  --build-arg APP_UID=$(id -u) --build-arg APP_GID=$(id -g)
```

Then add this stanza to `~/caddy/Caddyfile` and reload Caddy:

```
attrakttv.jemu.name {
    import common_log attrakttv
    reverse_proxy localhost:7842
}
```

```sh
cd ~/caddy && sudo caddy fmt --overwrite && sudo systemctl reload caddy
```

The app is then reachable at <https://attrakttv.jemu.name>.

### Update

```sh
ssh horst
cd ~/docker/attrakttv
git pull
docker compose up -d --build
```

The DESCRIPTION-only deps layer stays cached unless dependencies changed,
so code-only updates rebuild in seconds.

### Backup

```sh
tar czf attrakttv-data-$(date +%F).tar.gz -C ~/docker/attrakttv data/
```

State is one directory; tar is the whole story.

### Local Docker test

The same `docker-compose.yml` works on the dev machine:

```sh
cp attrakttv.env-sample .env && $EDITOR .env
mkdir -p data
docker compose up --build
```

Then open <http://127.0.0.1:7842>.
